extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and IP practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: A Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline (suspension) under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 following a state suspension, including procedural steps (notice, opportunity to respond, publication), temporary limited recognition, account restrictions, and conditions for reinstatement. The document sets the specific penalties, publishing requirements, and operational restrictions applicable to the suspended practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a State on ethical grounds; here, Respondent is suspended from practice before the USPTO for one (1) year for violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order applies the state-imposed sanction (one-year suspension) as the appropriate discipline in the absence of a successful defense under § 11.24(d). Action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice and opportunity to respond (40-day period) under § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'Notice and Order Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24' must be sent notifying the respondent and providing an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more reasons in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent files a timely response asserting one of the § 11.24(d)(1) defenses, the OED must consider it; failure to respond can result in a determination that there is no genuine issue of material fact and imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state's discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice when delivery unsuccessful
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Notice and Order cannot be delivered to the Respondent, the Notice must be published in the Official Gazette (example: published Dec 31, 2024 and Jan 7, 2025).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication in the Official Gazette serves as constructive notice where certified mail delivery cannot be effected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default consequence for failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, there is 'no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)' and reciprocal suspension (identical to the state discipline) is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-response permits the USPTO to resolve the proceeding on the record and impose the same discipline imposed by the state's authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited recognition under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f) for concluding client matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is granted limited recognition pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58(f) for thirty (30) days starting on the date of the Final Order so Respondent may endeavor to conclude work on behalf of clients on any matters pending before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If pending matters cannot be concluded within the 30-day limited recognition period, Respondent must advise each client so the client may make other arrangements; limited recognition is strictly time-limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order in OED FOIA Reading Room
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED's electronic FOIA Reading Room (http://foiadocuments.uspto.gov).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are publicly available at the OED FOIA Reading Room to provide public access and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette notice content requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided 'Notice of Suspension' text describing the Respondent, registration number, nature and duration of suspension, the regulation violated, and underlying state findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sample text includes: identification of respondent and registration number; statement that suspension is for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) predicated upon state suspension; summary of state findings and rules violated; and reference to availability of disciplinary decisions at the OED FOIA Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of misconduct warranting reciprocal discipline (state findings)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Arizona ruling found violations of Arizona Rules of Supreme Court 41(b)(7) and Rules of Professional Conduct ER 3.5(d), ER 8.2(a), and ER 8.4(d) by writing motions and other procedural documents containing inflammatory statements regarding the presiding judge and by filing frivolous counterclaims and motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order identifies specific types of conduct (inflammatory statements about a judge, conduct likely to disrupt a tribunal, making false statements about a judge's qualifications or integrity, conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice, filing frivolous claims/motions) as grounds that supported the state suspension and the reciprocal discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to disable or suspend USPTO.gov accounts after limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective the date of the expiration of the 30-day limited recognition, the USPTO is authorized to disable or suspend any USPTO.gov accounts registered to Respondent (including all accounts Respondent has ever established, sponsored, or used in connection with any trademark or patent matter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account disabling can be applied broadly to any account associated with the respondent; this is an enforcement mechanism to prevent further practice before USPTO systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to USPTO verified Electronic System accounts until reinstatement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for, obtain, or have his name added to a USPTO verified Electronic System account unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction bars the suspended practitioner from seeking verification or inclusion on accounts that would enable filings on USPTO systems until formal reinstatement under § 11.60.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on using or assisting with USPTO filing systems after limited recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediately upon expiration of the 30-day limited recognition, Respondent is prohibited from using, assessing, or assisting others in using or accessing any USPTO.gov account(s) or other USPTO filing systems for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ban applies to direct use, assessment, or assistance—preventing circumvention by using others' accounts after the limited period ends.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific prohibitions until reinstatement under § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: Until a petition for reinstatement is granted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.60, Respondent shall be prohibited (and USPTO is authorized to disallow) from: (1) opening or activating any USPTO.gov account(s) to be used for preparing or filing documents with the USPTO; (2) applying for, or attempting to apply for any USPTO.gov account(s); (3) verifying, or attempting to verify, any other person's credentials in connection with USPTO.gov account(s); and (4) sponsoring or attempting to sponsor USPTO.gov account(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerated list clarifies the forms of account-related activity that are barred until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No USPTO obligation to re-activate disabled/suspended accounts; respondent's responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing obligates the USPTO to sua sponte re-activate any USPTO.gov account disabled or suspended pursuant to the order; it is Respondent's sole responsibility to initiate any such re-activation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Re-activation requires affirmative action by the respondent after meeting reinstatement conditions; USPTO may but is not required to act on re-activation requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory/regulatory authority citation
rubrics_metrics.description: The action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citing the statute and regulation identifies the legal basis for reciprocal discipline and the USPTO's authority to impose professional sanctions for state-imposed ethical discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of service and methods of notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The Final Order must be served to parties: via certified mail, return receipt requested, to Respondent at the most recent address provided to the OED Director pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.11(a), and to an address of public record; and via e-mail to the OED Director or counsel as indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service methods (certified mail with return receipt and email to OED Director) are documented in a Certificate of Service to establish notice and administrative record of service.
